fakoli-doumbia.title: Fakoli
fakoli-doumbia.summary: Fakoli Doumbia was a blacksmith-clan leader and nephew of Soumaoro Kante in the Sundiata epic. When Soumaoro seized his wife Kere Kuba, Fakoli defected to Sundiata and his forces helped break the Sosso army at the battle of Krina. His descendants founded the Doumbia blacksmith lineage of Manden.

subcomandante-moises.title: Subcomandante Moisés
subcomandante-moises.summary: Subcomandante Moises is a Tseltal indigenous commander of the Zapatista Army of National Liberation (EZLN) in Mexico. He joined the organization in 1983, fought as an infantry major in the January 1994 uprising, served as right hand of Subcomandante Pedro, and in 2014 succeeded Subcomandante Marcos as the EZLN's public spokesperson.

frank-abagnale-sr..title: Frank Abagnale Sr.
frank-abagnale-sr..summary: Frank Abagnale Sr. (1914-1972) was a New York stationery businessman and the father of con artist Frank Abagnale Jr. He was his son's role model in salesmanship and worldly skill, and after divorcing he raised the boy alone for a time.

amamikyo.title: Amamikyu
amamikyo.summary: Amamikyo is the creation goddess of Ryukyuan (Amami-Okinawa) mythology. Ordered by the heavenly deity to make islands for gods to dwell on, she descended with earth and stones and first built Asumui at Kunigami Hedo, then established Seifa-utaki and the other sacred sites of the islands.

dae-joyeong.title: Go of Balhae
dae-joyeong.summary: Dae Joyeong (670-719) was the founding king of Balhae. When the Khitan revolt threw Liaodong into chaos, he led a group of Goguryeo and Mohe people east with his father Geolgeol Jungsang, defeated the pursuing Tang general Li Kaigu at the Tianmenling pass, and founded a state at Dongmo Mountain in 698, proclaiming it Jin (later Balhae).

anauakaq.title: Anaukaq Henson
anauakaq.summary: Anauakaq (1906-1987) was the Inuit son of the American Arctic explorer Matthew Henson, born in Greenland to an Inuit woman. Raised as a hunter after his father returned to America, he met his father's countrymen decades later and was received in the United States in 1987, where he saw his father's remains reinterred at Arlington.

hae-buru.title: Hae Buru
hae-buru.summary: Hae Buru was the founder of Dongbuyeo (Eastern Buyeo). Sonless into old age, he found a golden frog-shaped child at Gonyeon pond while sacrificing to the mountains and rivers, named him Geumwa, and made him crown prince; the Samguk Yusa records the lineage connecting him to the Buyeo royal house.

jibaekho.title: 지백호
jibaekho.summary: 지백호는 신라 건국 신화의 여섯 촌장 가운데 한 사람으로 화산에서 내려와 취산 진지촌의 촌장이 되었다. 알천 언덕의 회의에서 혁거세를 임금으로 추대하는 데 참여했고, 그의 촌은 뒤에 본피부가 되어 후손이 최씨 성을 받았다고 삼국유사는 전한다.

bram-van-der-kolk.title: Bram van der Kolk
bram-van-der-kolk.summary: Bram van der Kolk (born 1982) is a Dutch programmer who became lead developer of Megaupload. He met Kim Dotcom at twenty-one and ran the uploader rewards program and content-removal processing. He fought extradition to the United States for over a decade alongside Dotcom.

nadulu.title: Nadulu
nadulu.summary: Nadulu was a legendary leader of the Turkic tribes and the eldest of the four sons of Yizhi Nishidu in the Zhoushu account of the Ashina origin legend. He settled at Chujianshan, where he lit a fire that saved the freezing remnants of the A-pang-po band, and the people made him their chief.

okikurmi.title: Okikurmi (Ae-oyna-kamuy)
okikurmi.summary: Okikurmi (also Ae-oyna-kamuy) is a culture hero and kamuy of the Saru river region in Ainu mythology. He came down from the world of the kamuy, lived among people teaching them hunting, fishing, and millet farming, and in some traditions was driven back to the heavens when people failed to honor him.

lady-of-tushan.title: Lady of Tushan
lady-of-tushan.summary: The Lady of Tushan (Nujiao) was the wife of Yu the Great in Chinese legend. Yu took the daughter of the Tushan clan as his wife but left home four days later to continue taming the flood, and was absent even when she bore their son Qi. The Wu Yue Chunqiu and later texts preserve her story and her longing song for Yu.

xie.title: Xie of Shang
xie.summary: Xie (Qi) was the legendary ancestor of the Shang people. He aided Yu the Great in the flood control works, and Shun appointed him Minister of Instruction to teach the people and enfeoffed him at Shang with the surname Zi; his descendants, fourteen generations later, founded the Shang dynasty.

dardanus-of-troy.title: Dardanus (son of Zeus)
dardanus-of-troy.summary: Dardanus was the ancestor of the Trojan royal house. After his brother Iasion died he left Samothrace for the mainland opposite, where King Teucer gave him land and his daughter Bateia in marriage; he settled at the foot of Mount Ida and founded the line of Troy's kings.

abe-karatz.title: Abe Karatz
abe-karatz.summary: Abe Karatz, born Harold Karsten, was a disbarred lawyer and convicted embezzler who became Preston Tucker's promoter. He secured the acquiring securities firm and the giant Chicago plant for the Tucker Corporation, though his criminal past later damaged the company he promoted.

ousous.title: Sanchuniathon
ousous.summary: Ousous was a figure in the Phoenician History transmitted by Philo of Byblos. The text credits him as the first to cut a single tree, trim its branches, and put to sea, and to clothe himself in animal skins; later generations of Tyre honored him with a pillar and fire offerings.

lorne-knight.title: Lorne Knight
lorne-knight.summary: Lorne Knight (1893-1923) was an American explorer, the most Arctic-experienced member of the Wrangel Island expedition. Bedridden with scurvy, he was nursed by Ada Blackjack and died in June 1923 before rescue arrived; he was the expedition's last fatality.

naylamp.title: Naylamp
naylamp.summary: Naylamp is the legendary founder of the Lambayeque (Sican) culture of coastal Peru. Landing by balsa raft at the mouth of the Faquisllanga river with his wife Ceterni and retinue, he built a palace at Chot and installed the green stone idol Yampallec, founding a dynasty his descendants ruled until the sea swallowed the realm after Fempellec's transgression.

bu-eulla.title: 부을나
bu-eulla.summary: 부을나는 탐라 건국 신화에서 모흥혈에서 솟아 나온 세 신인 가운데 막내이다. 동쪽 바닷가에 떠온 나무 상자 속 벽랑국 처녀 하나와 혼인해 제삼도(지금의 북제주군 지역)에 자리를 잡았고, 탐라 부씨의 시조로 전한다.

nekuz.title: Ergenekon legend
nekuz.summary: Nekuz was a figure of the Turkic Ergenekon legend. Abu'l-Ghazi's account makes him a nephew of Il Khan who, with Il Khan's son Kayan, led the surviving Turks into the hidden valley of Ergenekon, where the people lived for four hundred years before a blacksmith melted the iron mountain and they came out to recover their homeland.

aio.title: Ibor and Aio
aio.summary: Aio, with his brother Ibor, co-led the Winnili out of Scandinavia southward in the Lombard origin legend recorded by Paul the Deacon's Historia Langobardorum. The people they led later became the Lombards who ruled Italy.

battus-i.title: Battus I of Cyrene
battus-i.summary: Battus I (7th-6th century BC) was the founder and first king of Cyrene. Stuttering, he went to Delphi to ask about his voice and was told instead to found a city in Libya; he led colonists from Thera, settled first on Platea island, then built Cyrene and founded the Battiad dynasty.

iztac-mixcoatl.title: Iztac Mixcoatl
iztac-mixcoatl.summary: Iztac Mixcoatl ('White Cloud Serpent') is the father of the Seven Caves in Central Mexican legend. Dwelling at Chicomoztoc with his wife Ilancueitl, he fathered the sons whose names became the Nahuatlaca peoples, the Xicalanca, Tenochca, and kindred nations of the migration traditions.

mahucutah.title: Popol Vuh
mahucutah.summary: Mahucutah was the third of the four men made of maize in the K'iche' Maya Popol Vuh, paired with the wife Tz'ununiha. He brought the god Hacavitz from Tulan and installed him; through his son Qo'ahau he became an ancestor of the Ahau K'iche' lineage.

chrobatos.title: Origin hypotheses of the Croats
chrobatos.summary: Chrobatos (Hrvatos) was one of the five brothers and two sisters who, in Constantine VII Porphyrogenitus's De Administrando Imperio, led the Croats out of White Croatia. The brothers Kloukas, Lobelos, Kosentzis, Mouchlo, and Chrobatos with the sisters Touga and Bouga crossed to Dalmatia and became the progenitors of the Croat people.

madghis-al-abtar.title: Butr
madghis-al-abtar.summary: Madghis al-Abtar is the ancestor of the Butr branch of Berbers in Ibn Khaldun's genealogy. From his descendants came the Zenata, Banu Ifran, and Maghrawa, from whom the Marinid and Zayyanid dynasties later branched off.

gun.title: Gun (Chinese mythology)
gun.summary: Gun was the father of Yu the Great in Chinese myth. When the flood rose to heaven he stole the Lord's self-swelling soil, Xirang, to dam the waters; for defying the command he was executed by Zhurong at Yu's outskirts, and from his corpse Yu was born to complete the flood control.

preah-thong.title: Preah Thong and Neang Neak
preah-thong.summary: Preah Thong (Hun-t'ien, Kaundinya) was the foreign prince of the Khmer foundation legend. Sailing to an uninhabited island he met the naga princess Neang Neak; grasping her garment he followed her under the water to the naga realm, married her, and received the land drained by the naga king as his realm, the origin of Funan.

kyi.title: Kyi, Shchek and Khoryv
kyi.summary: Kyi was the eldest of the legendary founders of Kyiv. With his brothers Shchek and Khoryv and sister Lybid he settled the hills above the Dnieper and built a town, which people called Kyiv after the eldest brother; he is named in the Primary Chronicle's foundation account.

malandela.title: Malandela kaLuzumana
malandela.summary: Malandela (c. 17th century) was the founder of the Zulu clan and father of Qwabe and Zulu. He settled below Mpembe hill with his wife Nozidiya; after his death the elder son Qwabe drove the herds out and founded his own clan, while Zulu remained and gave his name to the people who became the Zulu nation.

oleg-the-prophet.title: Oleg of Novgorod
oleg-the-prophet.summary: Oleg the Prophet (d. 912) was the Varangian prince who united Novgorod and Kyiv. After Rurik's death he took the young Igor south, lured out and killed Askold and Dir who ruled Kyiv in 882, made Kyiv 'the mother of Rus cities', and campaigned against Byzantium, nailing his shield to Constantinople's gates.

gugong-danfu.title: King Tai of Zhou
gugong-danfu.summary: Gugong Danfu (King Tai of Zhou) was the ancestor who moved the Zhou people to Qishan. When the Rong and Di attacked Bin for its goods, he chose not to fight and led his people away, crossing the Qi and Ju rivers over Mount Liang to settle below Qishan, where the Zhou grew toward kingship.

king-yan-of-xu.title: King Yan of Xu
king-yan-of-xu.summary: King Yan of Xu was the legendary benevolent ruler of the state of Xu. Born from an egg abandoned by a palace woman and warmed by a passerby's dog, he grew to rule with such ren that over thirty states submitted to him; when King Mu of Zhou attacked, he refused to let his people die and withdrew north, followed into exile by tens of thousands.

si-inthrathit.title: Si Inthrathit
si-inthrathit.summary: Si Inthrathit (1188-1270) was the first king of Sukhothai. Around 1238 Bang Klang Hao, lord of Bang Yang, joined Pha Mueang of Mueang Rat to seize Sukhothai from its Khmer administrator; Pha Mueang ceded the throne to him and he founded the Phra Ruang dynasty, father of Ram Khamhaeng.

panembahan-senapati.title: Senapati of Mataram
panembahan-senapati.summary: Panembahan Senapati (Sutawijaya, 1546-1601) founded the Mataram Sultanate of Java. The Babad Tanah Jawi says he went to the southern sea and made a pact with the Queen of the Southern Sea, Ratu Kidul, then destroyed Pajang and established Mataram's rule over Java.

sogolon-konde.title: Sogolon Kondé
sogolon-konde.summary: Sogolon Kondé was the mother of Sundiata Keita in the Mali epic. Taken as the price of a buffalo spirit slain by hunter brothers in Do, the hunchbacked woman was brought to King Naré Maghann of Niani; she bore Sundiata, endured the first queen's persecution, and went into exile with her son until his return.

zethus-of-thebes.title: Amphion and Zethus
zethus-of-thebes.summary: Zethus was the co-king of Thebes with his twin brother Amphion. Raised by a shepherd on Mount Cithaeron, the twins punished Lycus and Dirce for tormenting their mother Antiope, then took Thebes and built its walls, Zethus carrying stones by hand while Amphion's lyre drew them into place.

kambu-svayambhuva.title: Kambu Svayambhuva
kambu-svayambhuva.summary: Kambu Svayambhuva is the ascetic ancestor of the Khmer kings in the 947 Baksei Chamkrong inscription. By Shiva's blessing he won the apsara Mera as wife; from the pair came the Khmer royal line, and the country's name Kambuja was taken from Kambu.

vyatko.title: Vyatichi
vyatko.summary: Vyatko was the legendary chief of the Vyatichi. Parting from his brother Radim, he led his clan to the Oka river and settled there; the people of that land took the name Vyatichi from him, the Primary Chronicle relates.

dobun-mergen.title: Dobun Mergen
dobun-mergen.summary: Dobun Mergen was the husband of Alan Gua in the Secret History of the Mongols. Founding the Khorilar clan, he saw Alan Gua among a migrating band and took her as wife; she bore him Belgunutei and Bugunutei, and after his death her further sons became the ancestors of the Mongol tribes.

buqu-khan.title: Bögü Qaghan
buqu-khan.summary: Buqu Khan (Bogu Qaghan, r. 759-779) was the third qaghan of the Uyghur Khaganate. The Gaochang Wang Shehun stele tells that a tree sprang up overnight between the Tughla and Selenga rivers, its swelling like a pregnant woman's giving forth light, from which nine boys were born, the eldest of them Buqu who became khagan and adopted Manichaeism.

tur.title: Turan
tur.summary: Tur was the second son of Fereydun in the Shahnameh, receiving Turan and the eastern lands as his share, whence he was called Turshah. Conspiring with his brother Salm he killed their youngest brother Iraj; the peoples of Turan trace their line to him.

bamboo-king.title: Yelang
bamboo-king.summary: The Bamboo King (Zhutong) was the legendary founder of Yelang. A woman washing clothes at the Dun river saw a great three-jointed bamboo drift between her feet; hearing a cry inside she split it and found a boy, who grew to rule Yelang and took Zhu (bamboo) as his surname.

ma-drag-sinmo.title: Tibetan mythology
ma-drag-sinmo.summary: Ma Drag Sinmo (Srinmo) was the rock ogress of the Tibetan origin myth. She begged the meditating monkey, an emanation of Avalokiteshvara, for marriage; their six children became the ancestors of the Tibetan people, and the cave at Chetang in the Yarlung valley is preserved as the site.

awang-alak-betatar.title: Muhammad Shah of Brunei
awang-alak-betatar.summary: Awang Alak Betatar (d. 1402) was the first Sultan of Brunei. The Brunei royal genealogy says he settled by the Brunei river with his brothers; marrying the Johor princess Dayang Pingai he embraced Islam and took the name Muhammad Shah, opening Brunei's sultanate line.

hypsouranios.title: Sanchuniathon
hypsouranios.summary: Hypsouranios was Philo of Byblos's Greek rendering of Samemrum, meaning 'high heaven', in the Phoenician History. Settling at Tyre he first built dwellings of reeds, stalks, and papyrus, and after death was honored with his brother Ousous as a founder of Tyre.

ion.title: Ion (mythology)
ion.summary: Ion was the legendary ancestor of the Ionians. Son of Apollo and Creusa, he aided Athens in its war with Eleusis and divided the Athenians into four tribes; the people who followed him were called Ionians and carried his name to Asia Minor.

shinerikyo.title: Amamikyu
shinerikyo.summary: Shinerikyo is the male deity paired with Amamikyo in Ryukyuan creation myth. At the heavenly command he joined her in making the islands and placing people on them; their three sons and two daughters became the ancestors of the island peoples, the eldest son founding the royal line.

rus.title: Lech, Czech, and Rus
rus.summary: Rus is the legendary progenitor of the Rus' people. Parting from his brothers Czech and Lech, he went to the eastern plain and the people there took his name; the three-brother legend ties the origins of the Slavic nations together.

taibo-of-wu.title: Taibo
taibo-of-wu.summary: Taibo was the eldest son of Gugong Danfu who founded Wu. Perceiving that his father wished to pass the succession to his youngest brother Jili and Jili's son Chang, he withdrew to the Jingman lands with his brother Zhongyong, cut his hair and tattooed his body, and was welcomed by the local people as lord of Wu.

alpyeong.title: 알평
alpyeong.summary: 알평은 신라 건국 신화의 여섯 촌장 가운데 한 사람으로 하늘에서 표암봉에 내려와 알천 양산촌의 촌장이 되었다. 여섯 촌장과 알천 언덕에 모여 덕 있는 사람을 임금으로 세우자 의논하여 혁거세를 추대했다고 삼국유사는 전한다.

go-eulla.title: 고을나
go-eulla.summary: 고을나는 탐라 건국 신화에서 한라산 북쪽 모흥혈에서 솟아 나온 세 신인 가운데 한 사람이다. 가죽옷을 입고 사냥해 살다가 동쪽 바닷가에 떠온 나무 상자 속 벽랑국 처녀와 혼인해 제일도(지금의 제주시 일대)에 자리를 잡았고, 탐라 고씨의 시조로 전한다.

the-dragon-maiden.title: 원창왕후
the-dragon-maiden.summary: 원창왕후(용녀)는 고려 의조 작제건의 아내로 전하는 서해 용왕의 딸이다. 작제건을 따라와 개주 동북쪽에 자리 잡고 살았으며, 우물을 파고 그 길로 서해를 오갔다는 전설이 고려사 열전 등에 전한다.

iqui-balam.title: Popol Vuh
iqui-balam.summary: Iqui Balam was the youngest of the four men made of maize in the Popol Vuh, paired with the wife Caquixaha. He stood with the others when the gods were received at Tulan, but no descendants were allotted to him, so the youngest brother's line ended.

the-five-gaya-founder-brothers.title: 가락국기
the-five-gaya-founder-brothers.summary: 다섯 가야의 시조 형제는 가락국기에 전하는 인물들로, 구지봉의 금상자 속 여섯 알에서 나온 아이들 가운데 수로를 뺀 다섯이다. 각각 자기 땅으로 돌아가 대가야, 성산가야, 아라가야, 고령가야, 소가야의 임금이 되었다고 전한다.

yizhi-nishidu.title: Ashina tribe
yizhi-nishidu.summary: Yizhi Nishidu is an ancestor figure in the Zhoushu's second account of Ashina origins. A son of A-pang-po, chief of the Se kingdom north of the Xiongnu, he survived when the neighboring king slaughtered the band, fled with his brothers into the mountains, and became the forebear of the line from which the Turkic Ashina descended.

toi.title: Toi-te-huatahi
toi.summary: Toi (Toi-te-huatahi, Toi-kai-rakau) was a great chief of Hawaiki in Māori tradition. Setting out to find his grandson Whatonga who had not returned from sea, he reached Aotearoa and settled near Whakatane, becoming the ancestor claimed by the peoples of the eastern coast.

the-nine-gan.title: 가락국기
the-nine-gan.summary: 구간(九干)은 가락국기에 전하는 아도간·여도간·피도간·오도간·유수간·유천간·신천간·오천간·신귀간 아홉 사람이다. 임금 없이 백성을 나누어 다스리다 구지봉에서 하늘 소리가 나자 명에 따라 구지가를 부르고 춤추며, 내려온 금상자 속 수로를 임금으로 맞았다고 전한다.

yonggeon.title: Wang Ryung
yonggeon.summary: Yonggeon (Wang Ryung, 849-897) was Sejo of Goryeo, grandfather of the founder Taejo. Building a house south of Song'ak he met the monk Doson, heard that a sage would come from that land, and rebuilt as instructed; his lineage rose from local magnates to the Goryeo throne.

yngvi-freyr.title: Yngvi
yngvi-freyr.summary: Yngvi-Freyr was the legendary Swedish king in Snorri Sturluson's Ynglinga saga. Succeeding his father Njord he ruled Sweden and kept his temple and seat at Old Uppsala; after his death the people kept his mound holy and continued to invoke him for good harvests.

yekuno-amlak.title: Yekuno Amlak
yekuno-amlak.summary: Yekuno Amlak (r. 1270-1285) was the Ethiopian emperor who overthrew the Zagwe dynasty. Claiming descent from Menelik I, he declared the restoration of the Solomonic line and founded the dynasty that ruled Ethiopia until 1974.

borte-chino.title: Börte Chino
borte-chino.summary: Borte Chino ('grey wolf') is the ancestor of Genghis Khan named in the first section of the Secret History of the Mongols. With his mate Gua Maral he crossed the Tenggis and settled at the source of the Onon river by Burkhan Khaldun, beginning the Mongol royal genealogy.

jonathan-plummer.title: Jonathan Plummer
jonathan-plummer.summary: Jonathan Plummer (1761-1819) was a traveling peddler, preacher, and poet of Newburyport, Massachusetts. Taken up by the eccentric millionaire 'Lord' Timothy Dexter, he became his de facto poet laureate, writing laudatory verses and a biography of his patron.

amphion-of-thebes.title: Amphion and Zethus
amphion-of-thebes.summary: Amphion was the co-king of Thebes with his twin Zethus. Raised by a shepherd on Mount Cithaeron, the twins avenged their mother Antiope on Lycus and Dirce and took Thebes; building the walls, the stones moved into place of themselves at the music of the lyre Hermes gave Amphion.

bill-rusch.title: Brown Box
bill-rusch.summary: Bill Rusch is an MIT-trained engineer who joined Ralph Baer's 'Brown Box' team at Sanders Associates. He devised the circuit that let the machine itself control a third spot on the screen, enabling the first chase game and contributing key logic to what became the Magnavox Odyssey.

agasu.title: Agasu
agasu.summary: Agasu is the ancestral figure of the Fon and Allada royal lines. Fon tradition holds that the princess Aligbonu of Tado bore him by a leopard; his descendants left Tado, founded Allada, and from them branched the kings of Abomey (Dahomey) and Porto-Novo.

ainurakkur.title: Ainu mythology
ainurakkur.summary: Ainurakkur is the first god born on earth in Ainu mythology, son of the heavenly god and the elm-tree goddess Chikisani. Living in human form in the village, he taught the people to make bows and traps and the arts of hunting.

bak-hyeokgeose.title: Hyeokgeose of Silla
bak-hyeokgeose.summary: Bak Hyeokgeose (69 BC - 4 AD) was the founding king of Silla. The six village chiefs gathered on Alcheon hill, found a white horse kneeling by Najeong well and a red egg, from which a boy hatched; they raised him as king with the title Geoseogan, and his line founded the Park clan of Silla.

balam-quitze.title: Popol Vuh
balam-quitze.summary: Balam Quitze was the eldest of the four men made of maize in the Popol Vuh. Ground from white and yellow maize by the gods, he could see to the ends of the world until the gods blew mist over his eyes; he received the god Tohil at Tulan and became the ancestor of the Cauec K'iche'.

balla-fasseke-kouyate.title: Balla Fasséké Kouyaté
balla-fasseke-kouyate.summary: Balla Fasseke Kouyate was the griot of Sundiata Keita in the Mali epic and ancestor of the Kouyate griot line. Given to Sundiata by Naré Maghann, he was captured on a mission to Soumaoro, discovered the secret of the king's power in his palace, and escaped to warn Sundiata.

datuak-katumanggungan.title: Datuk Ketemanggungan
datuak-katumanggungan.summary: Datuak Katumanggungan was a legendary founder of Minangkabau custom. The Tambo Minangkabau makes him a son of Sri Maharaja Diraja, descendant of Iskandar Zulkarnain; he founded the Koto Piliang adat line, favoring hierarchy and strong leadership, against his half-brother's egalitarian Bodi Caniago.

datuak-parpatiah-nan-sabatang.title: Datuk Parpatih Nan Sabatang
datuak-parpatiah-nan-sabatang.summary: Datuak Parpatiah Nan Sabatang was a legendary founder of Minangkabau custom, the son of Sri Maharaja Diraja's widow by a second marriage. He opened the Agam region and chose a different path from his brother, founding the Bodi Caniago adat in which elders gather and decide by consensus.

dinga-cisse.title: Dinga Cissé
dinga-cisse.summary: Dinga Cissé was the legendary ancestor of the Cissé royal house of Wagadu (Ghana empire). Migrating from east to west he settled in the Wagadu land and took three wives; Soninke oral tradition says his youngest son by the third wife was promised to the seven-headed snake Bida.

djabe-cisse.title: Dyabe Cissé
djabe-cisse.summary: Djabe Cissé was the son of Dinga who founded Wagadu, capital of the Ghana empire. Inheriting his father's kingship he came to the Kumbi land and opened Wagadu; he made a pact with the seven-headed snake Bida of the well, offering a maiden each year in exchange for gold that made the realm rich.

gyeon-hwon.title: Gyeon Hwon
gyeon-hwon.summary: Gyeon Hwon (867-936) was the founder of Later Baekje. Born at Sangju's Gaeun county, he served as a Silla soldier guarding the southwest coast, then gathered followers, made Wansanju his capital, and proclaimed Later Baekje in 892, fighting Wang Geon for mastery of the peninsula until his sons' strife ended his power.

dakodonu.title: Dakodonu
dakodonu.summary: Dakodonu (d. 1645) was the legendary first king of Abomey. Entering the Abomey plateau he begged land of the chief Dan; mocked to take his belly instead, he killed Dan and built his palace on the grave, from which the kingdom took the name Dan-ho-me, 'in Dan's belly', Dahomey.

eri.title: Eri (king)
eri.summary: Eri was the legendary ancestor of the Nri kingdom of the Igbo. Tradition says he came down from the sky to the waterlogged land by the Anambra river, and Chukwu sent a smith to dry the land with his bellows; after Eri's death his son Nri founded the ritual kingship of Nri.

bartholomeus-welser.title: Bartholomeus Welser
bartholomeus-welser.summary: Bartholomeus Welser (1484-1561) was the head of the Augsburg Welser trading house, a merchant banker rivaling the Fuggers. Lending vast sums to Charles V, he received an imperial countship and the concession of Venezuela, which the Welsers exploited through their agents until the colony's venture collapsed.

gutae.title: 구태
gutae.summary: 구태는 주서와 수서에 전하는 대방 지역의 초기 통치자이다. 동명의 후손 가운데 어질고 미더운 사람으로 뽑혀 대방 옛 땅에 처음 나라를 세웠으며, 요동태수 공손도가 딸을 그의 아내로 삼았다고 전한다. 백제 건국 설화와 연결되는 인물이다.

isingoma-mpuga-rukidi.title: Rukidi I of Toro
isingoma-mpuga-rukidi.summary: Isingoma Mpuga Rukidi was the first Omukama of the Bito dynasty of Bunyoro. When the Chwezi king Wamara vanished he sent north into Luo country for the elder of Kyomya's twin sons; Rukidi came and received the kingship, founding the Bito line that ruled Bunyoro.

jakjegeon.title: Uijo of Goryeo
jakjegeon.summary: Jakjegeon (Uijo of Goryeo) was the father of Goryeo's founder Wang Geon in the dynasty's lineage legend. Sailing the western sea to find his father, he was left by sailors on an island where the dragon king gave him his daughter, the Lady Wonchang, in marriage; from them the Goryeo royal house descended.

jinui.title: 정화왕후
jinui.summary: 정화왕후 진의는 신라 하대의 왕후로 고려 왕실의 선조 여인이다. 언니가 오관산 꼭대기에서 오줌을 누어 천하에 넘치는 꿈을 꾸자 비단 치마를 주고 그 꿈을 샀고, 뒤에 당나라에서 온 귀인 작제건의 아내가 되어 의종 강충을 낳았다고 전한다.

linjun.title: Linjun
linjun.summary: Linjun (Lin Jun) was the legendary ancestor of the Ba people. From the red and black caves of Mount Wuluo Zhongli came the five surnames Ba, Fan, Shen, Xiang, and Zheng without a chief; in the contest to throw a sword into a rock crevice and float a clay boat, the Ba man won and was made Linjun, lord of the five clans.

carl-mark-force-iv.title: Carl Mark Force IV
carl-mark-force-iv.summary: Carl Mark Force IV (born 1969) was a corrupt US DEA agent on the Baltimore Silk Road task force. Using the undercover persona 'Nob' to contact Ross Ulbricht, he stole investigative bitcoin proceeds for himself; he was convicted and imprisoned for the theft.

edward-ciesielski.title: Edward Ciesielski
edward-ciesielski.summary: Edward Ciesielski (1922-1962) was a Polish underground activist. Arrested in January 1941 and imprisoned in Auschwitz as prisoner 12969, he joined the camp resistance and at twenty escaped in June 1942 in the famed commando-party breakout wearing SS uniforms.

kim-suro.title: Suro of Geumgwan Gaya
kim-suro.summary: Kim Suro (42-199) was the legendary founding king of Geumgwan Gaya. When a heavenly voice on Gujibong told the nine gans to sing and dance the Gujiga, a golden casket descended holding six eggs; the first to hatch, Suro, became king, and his brothers founded the other Gaya states.

ly-cong-uẩn.title: Lý Thái Tổ
ly-cong-uẩn.summary: Ly Cong Uan (974-1028) was the founding emperor of Vietnam's Ly dynasty. Succeeding the fallen Earlier Le dynasty in 1009, he moved the capital from Hoa Lu to Dai La the next year; a dragon seen rising as his ship arrived gave the new capital its name Thang Long, 'ascending dragon'.

fernando-yanez-munoz.title: Fernando Yáñez Muñoz
fernando-yanez-munoz.summary: Fernando Yanez Munoz, known as Comandante German, was a Mexican architect turned guerrilla leader. A founding member of the National Liberation Forces (FLN) in 1969, he established the EZLN's foothold in the Lacandon jungle in 1983 and recruited the man who became Subcomandante Marcos.

elizabeth-worrall.title: Elizabeth Worrall
elizabeth-worrall.summary: Elizabeth Worrall was the American-born wife of Samuel Worrall, a Gloucestershire magistrate. In 1817 she took in and sheltered at Knole Park the mysterious woman calling herself 'Princess Caraboo of Javasu', becoming a central figure in Britain's famous imposture episode.

nor.title: Nór
nor.summary: Nor was the legendary founding king of Norway in the Orkneyinga saga's Fundinn Noregr. Setting out to find his lost sister Goi, he parted from his brother Gor, crossed the snowy range southward, subdued the lands he passed, and gave his name to the land, Noregr (Norway).

gary-alford.title: Gary Alford
gary-alford.summary: Gary Alford was the US IRS special agent who identified Silk Road's operator. In 2013 a date-bounded Google search traced the earliest 'Altoid' posts promoting Silk Road to an account whose Gmail address exposed Ross Ulbricht, giving investigators the identity behind 'Dread Pirate Roberts'.

ito-tsurukichi.title: Ito Tsurukichi
ito-tsurukichi.summary: Ito Tsurukichi (1858-1913) was a Meiji-era interpreter-guide who accompanied Isabella Bird on her 1878 journey through interior Japan and Hokkaido. He is the 'Ito' of her Unbeaten Tracks in Japan, the indispensable companion of her travels.

george-w.-wheelwright-iii.title: George W. Wheelwright III
george-w.-wheelwright-iii.summary: George W. Wheelwright III (1903-2001) was a Harvard physics instructor who co-founded Polaroid. Joining his youngest student Edwin Land he formed the Land-Wheelwright laboratory, commercialized the polarizing sheet, and co-founded the Polaroid Corporation.

bunker-hunt.title: Nelson Bunker Hunt
bunker-hunt.summary: Nelson Bunker Hunt (1926-2014) was a son of the Hunt oil dynasty who, with his brothers, bought up much of the world's silver supply in an attempt to corner the market. When the market collapsed on 'Silver Thursday' in March 1980 the scheme failed and he was driven into bankruptcy.

alfreda-mitchell-bingham.title: Alfreda Mitchell Bingham
alfreda-mitchell-bingham.summary: Alfreda Mitchell Bingham (1874-1967), granddaughter of Tiffany's founder and wife of Hiram Bingham, was the patron of Machu Picchu's discovery. Her fortune funded her husband's Peru expeditions, and she raised seven sons while supporting his work.

arnaud-du-tilh.title: Arnaud du Tilh
arnaud-du-tilh.summary: Arnaud du Tilh (c. 1524-1560) was a Gascon peasant who in 1556 impersonated the missing Martin Guerre, living for three years with his house and wife Bertrande. His near-perfect performance persuaded a village until the real Martin returned; the trial became the celebrated case of Martin Guerre.

james-chuma.title: James Chuma
james-chuma.summary: James Chuma (c. 1850-1882), a Yao freed from slavery, became David Livingstone's faithful attendant. When Livingstone died in 1873, Chuma and Susi carried his body over 1,500 kilometers to the coast, bringing the explorer home for burial in Westminster Abbey.

madan-khatri-chhetri.title: Madan Khatri Chhetri
madan-khatri-chhetri.summary: Madan Khatri Chhetri (born 1955) was a legendary Nepali Army helicopter pilot. In the 1996 Everest disaster he twice flew to Camp 2 above 6,000 meters, an altitude thought to deny helicopters enough lift, rescuing survivors including Beck Weathers and Makalu Gau.

false-dmitry-i.title: False Dmitry I
false-dmitry-i.summary: False Dmitry I (d. 1606) was the first pretender of Russia's Time of Troubles. Claiming to be the dead Tsarevich Dmitry, he took the throne with Polish support and ruled ten months before being killed in a revolt; his ashes were reportedly fired from a cannon toward Poland.

jared-der-yeghiayan.title: Jared Der-Yeghiayan
jared-der-yeghiayan.summary: Jared Der-Yeghiayan was a US Homeland Security Investigations agent in the Chicago office who took over the Silk Road administrator account 'Cirrus', working undercover for three months on a bitcoin salary and helping close the net on Ross Ulbricht.

jan-redzej.title: Jan Redzej
jan-redzej.summary: Jan Redzej (1910-1944) was a Polish resistance member imprisoned in Auschwitz under the false name Jan Retko (number 5430). A member of the camp underground ZOW, he was one of the four prisoners who escaped in June 1942 in the celebrated commando-party breakout dressed as SS officers.

john-mulheren.title: John Mulheren
john-mulheren.summary: John Mulheren (1949-2003) was a brilliant arbitrageur who became a Merrill Lynch director at twenty-five and a close friend of Ivan Boesky. Feeling betrayed in 1988, he was arrested driving toward Boesky with rifles; the episode made him a Wall Street legend of the insider-trading era.

raleigh-rimmell.title: Raleigh Rimmell
raleigh-rimmell.summary: Raleigh Rimmell was a young Devon man and close friend of Jack Fawcett, Percy Fawcett's son. He accompanied the 1925 expedition seeking the lost city 'Z' and vanished with the Fawcetts in the Mato Grosso.

henry-costin.title: Henry Costin
henry-costin.summary: Henry Costin was a former British soldier and Percy Fawcett's most trusted expedition companion. He joined several Bolivia-Brazil border survey expeditions and shared jungle survival with Fawcett, though he did not join the fatal 1925 journey.

melchor-arteaga.title: Melchor Arteaga
melchor-arteaga.summary: Melchor Arteaga was a farmer of the Urubamba valley living below Machu Picchu. In 1911 he told Hiram Bingham of the Inca ruins on the ridge and personally guided him up the steep cliff, becoming the local guide of the discovery.

lilian-maclaughlin-brown.title: Lilian MacLaughlin Brown
lilian-maclaughlin-brown.summary: Lilian MacLaughlin Brown was an American writer and the second wife of dinosaur hunter Barnum Brown. Married in Calcutta, she joined fossil expeditions in India and Burma and turned the experience into her memoir 'I Married a Dinosaur'.

les-solomon.title: Les Solomon
les-solomon.summary: Les Solomon was the technical editor of Popular Electronics who catalyzed the personal computer revolution. He discovered Ed Roberts and the small Albuquerque firm MITS, put the Altair 8800 on the January 1975 cover, and thereby helped launch the industry.

ludwig-moyzisch.title: Ludwig Moyzisch
ludwig-moyzisch.summary: Ludwig Moyzisch (1905-1980s) was an Austrian journalist who, behind a commercial attache title at the Ankara embassy, directed SD operations in Turkey. He handled the British ambassador's valet Elyesa Bazna, 'Cicero', buying the photographed secrets that made the affair famous.

navarana-mequpaluk.title: Navarana Mequpaluk
navarana-mequpaluk.summary: Navarana Mequpaluk (1898-1921) was an Inuit woman of northwest Greenland and the first wife of Danish explorer Peter Freuchen. She accompanied his Arctic expeditions and bore two children; she died in the 1921 Spanish flu and was denied Christian burial as an unbaptized Inuk.

edward-barrill.title: Edward Barrill
edward-barrill.summary: Edward Barrill (1864-1909+) was a Montana mule driver, the sole companion of Frederick Cook's claimed 1906 first ascent of Mount McKinley. His 1909 sworn statement that the pair never neared the summit exposed Cook's claim as a fraud.

venetia-buddicom.title: Venetia Buddicom
venetia-buddicom.summary: Venetia Buddicom (born 1895) was an Englishwoman traveler and Freya Stark's closest friend. In 1928 she traveled with Stark through the Jebel Druze of French-mandate Syria and was briefly detained with her, the first of Stark's famous journeys.

kalian-singh.title: Pundit (explorer)
kalian-singh.summary: Kalian Singh was a Pundit explorer, cousin of Nain Singh, code-named 'G-K'. In the late 1860s he surveyed western Tibet in disguise, measuring the route from Ladakh to the Thok Jalung goldfield for the Great Trigonometrical Survey of India.

salim-bin-kabina.title: Salim bin Kabina
salim-bin-kabina.summary: Salim bin Kabina (born 1931) was a Bedouin of the Rashid tribe who, meeting Wilfred Thesiger in 1945-46 at seventeen, became the only companion present on all the explorer's Arabian journeys, including the Empty Quarter crossings.

talbot-edwards.title: Talbot Edwards
talbot-edwards.summary: Talbot Edwards (born c. 1594) was the aged keeper of the Crown Jewels in the Tower of London's Martin Tower. Showing the regalia to visitors for a fee, the seventy-seven-year-old befriended 'parson' Thomas Blood, who in 1671 used the trust to attempt the theft of the Crown Jewels.

gerald-cotten.title: Gerald Cotten
gerald-cotten.summary: Gerald Cotten (1988-2018) founded Canada's largest cryptocurrency exchange, QuadrigaCX. Announced dead of Crohn's complications on an India honeymoon, he took the keys to $250 million of customer funds with him; the exchange's collapse exposed a Ponzi-like scheme.

william-hall-walker.title: William Walker, 1st Baron Wavertree
william-hall-walker.summary: William Hall Walker (1856-1933) was a Liverpool brewing heir, amateur photographer, and nineteen-year MP who became Baron Wavertree. Befriending George Eastman he headed Kodak's British company, and founded the Tully stud that became Ireland's National Stud, pioneering racehorse breeding.

frank-brownell.title: Frank Brownell
frank-brownell.summary: Frank Brownell (1859-1939) was a Canadian wood craftsman making cameras in Rochester whom George Eastman engaged; he designed most of the early Kodak cameras, including the one-dollar 'Brownie' that put photography in everyone's hands.

josefa-macgregor.title: Gregor MacGregor
josefa-macgregor.summary: Josefa MacGregor, born Josefa Aristeguieta, was a Caracas heiress and cousin of Simon Bolivar. Marrying Gregor MacGregor in 1812, she played the 'Cacica of Poyais' in London society, lending respectability to her husband's fictional-country fraud until her death in 1838.

john-eacott-manahan.title: John Eacott Manahan
john-eacott-manahan.summary: John Eacott Manahan (1919-1990) was a University of Virginia historian and genealogist, Charlottesville's notable eccentric. In 1968 he married Anna Anderson, who claimed to be Grand Duchess Anastasia, and championed her identity claim for the rest of his life.

felix-schanzkowsky.title: Franziska Schanzkowska
felix-schanzkowsky.summary: Felix Schanzkowsky was a Polish laborer, brother of Franziska Schanzkowska, the woman identified as Anna Anderson's true self. Confronted with Anderson in 1927 he gave the ambiguous verdict of 'strong resemblance', neither confirming nor denying the claimant was his sister.

angele-egwuna.title: Angele Egwuna
angele-egwuna.summary: Angele Egwuna (born 1890) was an Ojibwe woman of Lake Temagami, Ontario. Marrying the English youth Archibald Belaney in 1910 she taught him Ojibwe language, canoeing, and trapping; he later reinvented himself as 'Grey Owl', the conservationist persona she helped make possible.

bartus-korteling.title: Bartus Korteling
bartus-korteling.summary: Bartus Korteling (1853-1930) was a Dutch painter and art teacher. To his pupil Han van Meegeren he taught Vermeer's technique and pigment preparation and instilled a love of the seventeenth-century masters, unknowingly schooling the century's greatest forger.

kinshichi-kozuka.title: Kinshichi Kozuka
kinshichi-kozuka.summary: Kinshichi Kozuka (1922-1972) was a former Imperial Japanese Army corporal and Hiroo Onoda's last comrade on Lubang Island. After Akatsu's surrender in 1950 and Shimada's death in 1954 he stayed alone with Onoda until police killed him in October 1972, leaving Onoda the last holdout.

jean-caneri.title: Popski's Private Army
jean-caneri.summary: Jean Caneri, called 'Jan', was one of the three founders of 'Popski's Private Army'. Serving with Peniakoff and Yunnie in the Libyan Arab Force, he became the photography officer of the minimal independent unit raiding behind Axis lines in North Africa and Italy.

boris-shikhmuradov.title: Boris Shikhmuradov
boris-shikhmuradov.summary: Boris Shikhmuradov (born 1949) was a Turkmen diplomat, a Soviet foreign service officer who became his country's foreign minister 1995-2000. Breaking with Niyazov he led the opposition; after the November 2002 coup attempt he was seized, given a show confession on television, sentenced to life, and vanished into prison.

lattie-tipton.title: Lattie Tipton
lattie-tipton.summary: Lattie Tipton (1911-1944) was a US Army soldier and Audie Murphy's closest comrade. Refusing promotion to sergeant to stay Murphy's runner, he shared foxholes from the Sicily landing until he was killed by a German sniper in August 1944 while at Murphy's side.

richard-chichakli.title: Richard Chichakli
richard-chichakli.summary: Richard Chichakli (born 1959) is a Syrian-born American accountant who, after US Army service and a Texas CPA practice, became 'financial manager' for arms dealer Viktor Bout. Indicted with Bout and long a fugitive, he was arrested in Australia in 2013 and convicted in the United States.

lyn-ulbricht.title: Lyn Ulbricht
lyn-ulbricht.summary: Lyn Ulbricht (born 1954) is an American libertarian activist. When her son Ross Ulbricht received a double life sentence for Silk Road she built the 'Free Ross' campaign, leading it for over a decade until his presidential pardon in 2025.

akira-iwanaga.title: Akira Iwanaga
akira-iwanaga.summary: Akira Iwanaga was a Mitsubishi Heavy Industries engineer and colleague of Tsutomu Yamaguchi. Caught in the Hiroshima bombing on a business trip in August 1945, he returned home to Nagasaki and endured the second bomb three days later, a twice-bombed survivor never officially recognized like Yamaguchi.

takahashi-kageyasu.title: Takahashi Kageyasu
takahashi-kageyasu.summary: Takahashi Kageyasu (1785-1829) was the Edo shogunate's astronomer and a rangaku scholar. He supervised completion of Ino Tadataka's surveyed map of Japan and founded a translation bureau; giving the map to Philipp von Siebold brought the 'Siebold Incident', for which he was imprisoned and died.

paul-kipfer.title: Paul Kipfer
paul-kipfer.summary: Paul Kipfer (1905-1980) was a Swiss physicist and Auguste Piccard's assistant. In May 1931 he rode the pressurized gondola balloon from Augsburg to 15,785 meters, becoming with Piccard the first human to enter the stratosphere.

dan.title: Gesta Danorum
dan.summary: Dan was the legendary ancestor of the Danes. Saxo Grammaticus opens the Gesta Danorum by making Dan and Angul the two sons of Humble, progenitors of the Danish people; Dan gave his name to the nation and began the line of Danish kings.

deganawidah.title: Deganawidah
deganawidah.summary: Deganawidah, the Great Peacemaker, was the Huron-born prophet who founded the Haudenosaunee. Crossing Lake Ontario in a white stone canoe, he walked with Hiawatha to bring the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga, and Seneca into the Great Law of Peace.

jean-louis-blondeau.title: Jean-Louis Blondeau
jean-louis-blondeau.summary: Jean-Louis Blondeau is a French photographer and Philippe Petit's longtime co-conspirator. After Notre-Dame and Sydney Harbour Bridge he helped plan the 1974 World Trade Center twin-towers wire walk, the 'coup', and photographed it from the roof.

seok-talhae.title: Talhae of Silla
seok-talhae.summary: Seok Talhae (d. 80 AD) was the fourth king of Silla and ancestor of its Seok clan. Born in an egg to the queen of Yongseong's Hamdalpawa and set adrift in a chest, he was found by the old woman Ajin at Ajinpo; he later won the throne by the trick of the crushed pebbles, legend says.

geraldine-apponyi.title: Geraldine of Albania
geraldine-apponyi.summary: Geraldine Apponyi (1915-2002), of the Hungarian Apponyi counts, was Albania's last queen. Working as a Budapest department-store clerk she married King Zog I in 1938 and was called 'the White Rose of Hungary'; after the Italian invasion she lived the rest of her life in exile.

tacaynamo.title: Tacaynamo
tacaynamo.summary: Tacaynamo was the legendary first ruler of Chimor on Peru's north coast. Arriving by balsa raft on the Moche valley shore, he announced that a great lord had sent him to rule the land, scattered yellow powder as a sign, and founded the dynasty that built Chan Chan.

con-ticci-viracocha.title: Viracocha
con-ticci-viracocha.summary: Con Ticci Viracocha is the creator god of Andean tradition. Emerging into a world of darkness he raised the sun, moon, and stars from Lake Titicaca, shaped model humans from stone, and brought the peoples forth from the springs, caves, and rocks of each district.

max-clausen.title: Max Clausen
max-clausen.summary: Max Clausen (1899-1979) was a German communist and GRU radio operator. In Shanghai and Tokyo he ran the transmitter of the Richard Sorge spy ring, the ring's sole link to Moscow; arrested in 1941 he survived the war in Japanese prison.

ootah.title: Ootah
ootah.summary: Ootah (1878-1955) was an Inuit hunter of northwest Greenland. One of the five men claimed to have reached the North Pole on Peary's 1909 expedition, he was held the finest dog driver of the party.

paul-goillot.title: Paul Goillot
paul-goillot.summary: Paul Goillot (1914-1987) was a Paris-born SOE and OSS operative in the French Resistance during the Second World War. Working operations alongside Virginia Hall in Haute-Loire he became her partner and later husband.

guryema.title: 구례마
guryema.summary: 구례마는 신라 건국 신화의 여섯 촌장 가운데 한 사람으로 이산에서 내려와 무산 대수촌의 촌장이 되었다. 알천 모임에서 혁거세를 임금으로 세우는 데 참여했고, 그의 촌이 점량부로 바뀌면서 후손이 손씨 성을 받았다고 삼국유사는 전한다.

robert-park-yunnie.title: Robert Park Yunnie
robert-park-yunnie.summary: Robert Park Yunnie (1909-1961) was the first recruit and deputy commander of 'Popski's Private Army'. Peniakoff's friend since the Libyan Arab Force, he led B Patrol through the North African and Italian raids of the celebrated private unit.

three-princesses-of-byeollang.title: 삼성혈
three-princesses-of-byeollang.summary: 벽랑국 세 공주는 탐라 건국 신화의 세 왕비이다. 동쪽 바닷가에 떠온 나무 상자 안에서 푸른 옷을 입은 세 처녀가 오곡 씨앗과 송아지, 망아지와 함께 있었고, 모흥혈의 세 신인과 혼인해 탐라 고씨·양씨·부씨의 기원이 되었다고 전한다.

sofya-nedyuzheva.title: Sofya Nedyuzheva
sofya-nedyuzheva.summary: Sofya Nedyuzheva (born 1742) was a Don Cossack woman who married Yemelyan Pugachev in 1760 and bore him three children. When her husband raised the great rebellion pretending to be Peter III, she became the government's hostage, imprisoned during and after the revolt.

alasha-khan.title: Alash (khan)
alasha-khan.summary: Alasha Khan is a figure of Kazakh legend. Born with a mottled (alash) body to the khan and cast out, he was raised by an old woman on the steppe; grown, he gathered a following, was raised on felt in the custom reserved for khans, and gave his name to the Alash, the Kazakh horde and self-name.

ayar-uchu.title: Ayar Brothers
ayar-uchu.summary: Ayar Uchu was one of the four Ayar brothers of the Inca origin legend. Walking with his brothers from Pacaritambo, at the council of Quirirmanta the brothers resolved to leave him on Huanacauri hill; he turned to stone there and became the sacred huaca of Huanacauri.

wanyan-aguda.title: Emperor Taizu of Jin
wanyan-aguda.summary: Wanyan Aguda (1068-1123), seventh-generation descendant of Hanpu, became chief of the Wanyan in 1113. Rising against the Liao the next year, he broke the Liao army at Chuhedian and took Ningjiangzhou; in 1115 he proclaimed himself emperor and founded the Jin dynasty that destroyed Liao.

ayar-auca.title: Ayar Brothers
ayar-auca.summary: Ayar Auca was the Ayar brother who stayed with Manco Capac to the end in the Inca origin legend. Reaching the Cusco valley, Manco sent him ahead to claim the land; he took possession and turned into a stone pillar, becoming the huaca of the Coricancha.

fekulen.title: Bukūri Yongšon
fekulen.summary: Fekulen was the youngest of the three heavenly maidens of the Manchu origin legend. Bathing in the Bulhuri pool northeast of Mount Changbai, she ate the red berry a magpie laid on her clothes, conceived, and bore Bukuri Yongson, ancestor of the Aisin Gioro line.

yang-eulla.title: 양을나
yang-eulla.summary: 양을나는 탐라 건국 신화에서 모흥혈에서 솟아 나온 세 신인 가운데 한 사람이다. 벽랑국 상자에서 나온 처녀와 혼인해 제이도(지금의 서귀포 지역)에 자리를 잡았고, 탐라 양씨의 시조로 전한다.

yao.title: Emperor Yao
yao.summary: Yao was the legendary sage king who began the abdication succession. Making virtue bright he harmonized the nine clans, charged the Xi and He to observe sun, moon, and stars to fix the four seasons for the people's farming, and in old age passed the throne not to his son but to the worthy Shun.

valentin-savitsky.title: Valentin Savitsky
valentin-savitsky.summary: Valentin Savitsky (born 1926) was the Soviet Navy captain of submarine B-59. On 27 October 1962, at the height of the Cuban Missile Crisis, under US depth-charge attack he judged war had already begun and prepared to fire the nuclear torpedo; Vasili Arkhipov's refusal prevented it.
